For reports of fibrotic reactions occurring in patients with Parkinson’s disease receiv- ing ergot derivative dopamine agonists including bromocriptine, see Fibrosis, below. Effects on sexual function. For reports of the effects of dopamine agonists on sexual function, see under Levodopa, p.806. Effects on the urinary tract. Constant dribbling urinary in- continence developed in a woman receiving bromocriptine 2.5 mg daily for a recurrent pituitary growth; symptoms resolved on stopping the drug and recurred on rechallenge.1 Bromocrip- tine has been shown to have two effects, one on the bladder out- flow tract and one on the detrusor muscle, that could predispose to urinary incontinence.2 1.
